levelMapping: SDE II = L5 (≈ Google L4); Amazon's own band is roughly 3–6 YOE but offers for ~3 YOE are routinely downlevelled to SDE I (L4) after the debrief — several 2025–2026 reports with 2.5–3.3 YOE were offered SDE I after a weak HLD or Bar Raiser round. Recruiters tell sub-4-YOE candidates they must 'convince the panel' on design depth; L5 interviews for ~3 YOE are realistic in India via referral/recruiter but the design rounds decide the level, not the coding rounds.

process.summary: Amazon runs the most standardised FAANG loop: OA (HackerRank; 2 coding + work-simulation + work-style survey; since mid-2026 many SDE packets replace one coding problem with a 60-minute AI-assisted bug-fixing task in a small repo) → 60-min phone screen (1–2 LeetCode mediums + 1–2 Leadership Principle questions, eliminatory) → a 4–5 round loop of 60 minutes each: 1–2 DSA rounds, one 'Logical & Maintainable' LLD/OOD round, one System Design (HLD) round usually taken by the hiring manager, and a Bar Raiser from another org whose format varies (pure LP, LP + a hard DSA problem, or LP + HLD). Every loop round spends 15–30 minutes on 2 Leadership Principle stories with aggressive follow-ups and these are scored, not warm-up; in 2026 almost every round also asks one 'how do you use GenAI / how do you verify AI-generated code' question. Decisions are made in a single debrief after all rounds; 'design depth' is the stated rejection or downlevel reason in most SDE II failures.

rounds.name: Online Assessment (HackerRank)
rounds.duration: 90–120 min for SDE II (coding 70–90 min + work simulation 15–60 min + work-style survey ~10 min)
rounds.what: Classic packet: 2 coding problems (one Medium, one Medium/Hard; often custom-worded Amazon-flavoured statements — shipments, warehouses, parcels, permutations), then a work-simulation (respond to inbox/chat scenarios, rank options against Leadership Principles; SDE II packets add 20 min of 'system design scenario' MCQs) and a two-statement work-style survey. New 2026 packet seen in SDE/SDE II reports from Jun–Aug 2026: ONE DSA problem (40 min, often binary-search-on-answer / medium-hard) + a 60-min 'Agentic/AI-assisted coding' task: a small web-app repo (choose Node/MERN, Java Spring Boot or Python/Django) with 3 bugs and a built-in AI assistant that explains code and locates files but refuses to hand you the fix.
rounds.probes: Passing all tests is not required to advance (reports of 11/15 and 4/6 passing and still moving on). OA scores are reused across roles — the loop call can come 1–4 months later. Copy/paste and browser activity are logged; print-screen ends the session; unauthorised GenAI is grounds for disqualification. Senior/referred candidates are sometimes allowed to skip the OA.

rounds.name: Phone screen (technical)
rounds.what: One engineer; ~45 min coding (1–2 LeetCode-medium problems, e.g. Subarray Sum Equals K, Capacity To Ship Packages, Word Break I+II, Optimal Account Balancing, Stepping Numbers, Find All Anagrams, Number of Islands with diagonals) and ~15 min on 1–2 LPs (Bias for Action, Ownership, Dive Deep are common). Eliminatory; result within ~2 days.
rounds.probes: Brute-force → optimal narrative, time/space complexity, dry run on edge cases, and 2–3 follow-up variants of the same problem (e.g. sum of each window → max of each window). Explaining a correct sub-optimal approach and how to improve it has been enough to pass.

rounds.name: Loop: Coding / Problem Solving (1–2 rounds)
rounds.what: Usually 2 problems (one Medium warm-up, one Medium/Hard) or one problem with escalating follow-ups; Amazon-tagged top-100 is the pool but statements are re-skinned (Koko 'in a different context', Rotting Oranges variants, Making A Large Island, Trapping Rain Water as a follow-up to Container With Most Water, custom BFS that grows into multi-source BFS). Working code in a plain shared editor (Amazon Chime + LiveCode/CodePair) is expected; no compiler.
rounds.probes: Interviewers are told to drive to an optimal solution and ask for complexity after each step; a space-optimisation follow-up is standard. Unfinished code in the second problem is survivable if the approach was explained, but the Bar Raiser is less forgiving. Candidates who stayed silent about an edge case they knew were marked down.

rounds.name: Loop: Logical & Maintainable code (LLD / OOD)
rounds.what: Open-ended, deliberately vague prompt (Amazon Locker and its 'reverse' return-drop variant, meeting-room scheduler, parking lot with pricing models, notification service, file-system search/filter library, rate limiter, issue/ticket management, digital wallet, tic-tac-toe, elevator). Expectation varies by interviewer: UML + class skeletons on Bluescape/Excalidraw, or working code for 2–3 core methods, or (increasingly in India) API + DB schema design that looks like mini-HLD.
rounds.probes: Requirement gathering (10–15 min), choosing entities, SOLID and 1–2 named design patterns (Strategy, Observer, State, Factory), extensibility ('add a new severity level / locker size / channel'), concurrency (double booking, two users taking the last unit), and data-structure choice for the core lookup. Drifting into HLD is a frequently cited failure; so is naming LRU without implementing it.

rounds.name: Loop: System Design (HLD) — usually with the Hiring Manager
rounds.duration: 60 min (sometimes 90–105 min; 20–30 min LPs/project deep-dive + 30–40 min design)
rounds.what: One product-shaped prompt, often from the team's own domain (Devices: config sync / backup & restore between old and new devices; Prime Video/Music: news feed, music streaming; Retail: inventory, cart, Diwali-load website, locker; Kindle: book recommendations) or a classic (news feed, URL shortener, BookMyShow, rate limiter, WhatsApp, payment service, auction platform). Happy path first, then failure modes.
rounds.probes: Functional/non-functional requirements and back-of-envelope numbers (defend them), API + schema, SQL vs NoSQL justification, caching/CDN, push vs pull fan-out, the celebrity/hot-key problem, concurrency and overselling (locks, transactions, idempotency keys), offline devices and retries, monitoring/alerting, cost. HM rounds also spend 20–35 min on LPs (Ownership, Deliver Results, Earn Trust) and product-judgement questions.

rounds.name: Bar Raiser
rounds.what: Senior engineer/manager from a different org, trained and with veto power; reads earlier rounds' notes. Format is interviewer's choice: (a) 45–60 min pure LP deep-dive (most common in 2025–2026 India reports), (b) 10–15 min LPs + one Hard DSA problem (Knapsack-style, Find the Safest Path in a Grid, Magnetic Force Between Two Balls, Earliest Moment Everyone Becomes Friends/DSU, LCS variant, 'here is brute-force code — explain it then optimise it'), or (c) LPs + HLD/LLD (Amazon Locker, BookMyShow, low-latency API over S3 data).
rounds.probes: Consistency and diversity of stories (do not reuse earlier rounds' stories), quantified impact, what you would do differently, your questions to the interviewer are evaluated. Coding here demands finished, dry-run code — several SDE II rejections/downlevels cite incomplete Bar Raiser code.

rounds.name: Debrief + recruiter decision
rounds.duration: 2–5 business days after the last round (often same week)
rounds.what: Interviewers vote Hire/No-Hire per LP evidence; Bar Raiser speaks last. Recruiters in India frequently relay per-round feedback ('Inclined / Not inclined') and will say explicitly if the panel wants to downlevel to SDE I or offer a contract/SysDev role instead.
rounds.probes: Design depth (LLD + HLD) decides L5 vs L4 far more often than DSA; LP coverage gaps in Customer Obsession/Ownership are the typical Bar Raiser veto.

process.indiaNotes: Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai run the identical loop (OA → phone screen → 4–5 rounds + Bar Raiser) and the same Leadership-Principle weighting; differences are logistical: (1) rounds are commonly bunched 2–3 per day, and Amazon India often runs face-to-face 'hiring drives' on campus where LLD/HLD are done on paper or on Bluescape (practise Bluescape — multiple candidates found it awkward); (2) a 'Logical & Maintainable' LLD round is almost always present and Indian interviewers increasingly ask for API + DB schema rather than pure class design; (3) reschedules and multi-week gaps are endemic — every round rescheduled at least once in several reports — and late-evening (9–11 pm IST) slots with US interviewers are common; (4) ~3 YOE candidates are interviewed for L5 but downlevels to SDE I are frequent, and recruiters may offer FTC (12-month contract) or SysDev-2 alternatives; (5) Indian loops report heavier LP time (often 30 min of a 60-min round). US/EU loops seen (Seattle, NY, Dublin) sometimes have 3 coding + 1 LLD and no HLD at mid-level, or a dedicated full-behavioural round; the UK/EU phone screen is more often a single problem. Language is free (Java most common among interviewers; Python/Go accepted but one Go candidate had to explain syntax).
process.timeline: OA to loop call: 2 weeks to 4 months (OA scores are pooled across roles). Phone screen to loop: 1–2 weeks. Loop: 1–4 weeks (India: often spread over 2–6 weeks because of reschedules). Decision: 2–5 business days after the Bar Raiser. End-to-end typically 4–8 weeks; fast-tracked to ~2–3 weeks when a competing offer exists. Reapply cool-off after a loop rejection is usually 6 months (one report said 6–24 months).
tips: Prepare 8–10 STAR stories with numbers mapped to all 16 LPs (two per LP for the big six: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Dive Deep, Deliver Results, Earn Trust, Bias for Action); never reuse a story across rounds — the Bar Raiser reads prior notes.
Ask the recruiter which 2 LPs each round covers and whether the design round is LLD or HLD; a mislabelled round (LLD vs HLD) caused a neutral/negative result in two 2026 reports.
In LLD, spend ≤10 min on requirements, name entities, then write real classes and 2–3 core methods; if you mention LRU/token bucket, be ready to implement it. Do not drift into HLD.

In HLD, defend your capacity estimates, build the happy path, then volunteer failure modes (offline device, hot key, double booking, retries/idempotency) before the interviewer asks; expect concurrency/overselling in anything inventory-, booking- or locker-shaped.
Expect a GenAI question in every 2026 round: have one specific story of using an AI tool, how you verified its output, and one case where you chose not to use it.
Coding: say the brute force, move to optimal, state complexity, dry-run on the given input, and mention edge cases out loud; start coding by minute 20 even if the optimum is unclear.

For the new OA: pick the stack you actually know (Django/Spring/MERN), read failing tests first, ask the AI assistant narrow questions, keep patches minimal, and leave the 40-min DSA problem no fumble room.
Practise Amazon-tagged problems by frequency (30-day/3-month tags) but drill variants: windows → max of window, BFS → multi-source BFS → Dijkstra, LIS → bounded-gap LIS, locker → size-tiered locker.
Log in to Bluescape/LiveCode before the slot; India rounds are often at night with US interviewers who join late — budget time.
If downlevelled to SDE I, ask the recruiter for an extra HLD round; it is usually refused but the ask documents the gap.
process.notes: OA platform: HackerRank (Amazon-branded); supported languages include C, C++, Java, Python, JS, Go, Kotlin. AI-assisted coding: appears ONLY in the OA (2026 'agentic coding' / repo bug-fix section with a sandboxed assistant that will not write the fix); no live loop round allows AI, and recruiters state that unauthorised GenAI use in the OA or loop is disqualifying — several candidates say interviewers reject on suspicion alone. What DID change in live rounds in 2026 is a scored GenAI-literacy behavioural question in most rounds and 'GenAI-focus' hiring-manager rounds. Whiteboarding: Bluescape (Amazon internal) or Excalidraw for design; Amazon Chime + LiveCode for code, no compiler. Bar Raiser can be any format and has veto. No separate 'values' round — LPs are embedded everywhere. The ~2000 Amazon-tagged LeetCode problems make the pool wide; 2025–2026 reports cluster on binary-search-on-answer, grid/multi-source BFS, sliding window, heaps/top-K streams, tree DP, intervals, and LRU/LFU design.

A buy matches the cheapest sell with price ≤ buy price; a sell matches the highest buy with price ≥ sell price; partial fills reduce qty. After processing, return the total quantity across orders that could not be matched (example given returns 6). Use a max-heap of buys and a min-heap of sells; watch 1e9 quantities.

dsa.statement: Given a lowercase string, change the minimum number of characters so it becomes a palindrome; among all minimum-change results return the lexicographically smallest. For each mismatched mirror pair pick the smaller character; then (optional second pass) if fewer than k changes were used, turn pairs into 'a' from the left.

You may upgrade exactly one warehouse to absorb the batch while every other warehouse still meets its backup threshold. Decide feasibility or the minimum upgrade cost. Sort capacities and check thresholds greedily; also know the 'count points within total distance d of all centres' variant (sum of |x - c_i| ≤ d, binary search both ends).

dsa.statement: You get a small web application repo (choose Node/MERN, Java Spring Boot or Python/Django) with a preview of the running site and ~3 failing behaviours/tests; fix them in 60 minutes. A sandboxed AI assistant can explain code and point to files but refuses to give the fix.
